answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting. Each epoch, an identity's action timing, payload size, and peer-selection vectors are hashed into a crystal reference profile stored as a compact digest. A ferrous anchor commits that digest into the next epoch's ledger, so an attacker reusing one identity across epochs must reproduce prior behaviour with copper-level tolerance or the digest mismatch voids all accrued reputation. Sybil swarms thus pay one full behavioural replay per identity per epoch, raising cost linearly with swarm size.
